name: core
description: v2.42.0 (2026-07-28) - Two Stop-layer fixes reach the fleet. (1) blueprint-check.sh v3 is TEXT-FIRST (#81): it validates the BLUEPRINT block in the turn's response text -- the block the user actually sees -- instead of the .claude/blueprint-registered marker. Emitting a correct block now unblocks Edit/Write; the marker becomes a per-turn cache the hook writes for itself. PreToolUse enforcement narrows to FOUNDATIONAL paths (now configurable via per_turn_blocks.blueprint.foundational_paths in sutra-defaults.json, overridable per repo with blueprint_foundational_paths[] in .claude/sutra-project.json); ordinary files are floored at Stop by per-turn-hard-gate.sh on any turn that mutated a governed file. Closes the divergence behind #68, the 2026-07-08 Testlify incident and its 2026-07-27 repeat. (2) h-sutra-enforce.sh v8/v9 + flow-stop-check.sh honor .profile (#72): DIRECTION-VERB is now case-insensitive (Postel's law -- emit UPPERCASE, accept any case), and only profile=company gets a forced redo; individual/project/unknown get warn+log. Fail-open by design -- no sutra-project.json or no jq means warn, never a hard block. The 'Enforce: warn-only' banner is finally true for the loud layers. (3) Release hygiene: the marketplace.json catalog had drifted to 2.39.20 while source was 2.41.2 -- both now say 2.42.0, and test-validate-manifest-json.sh passes again. + v2.40.0 (2026-07-20) - D63: per-turn governance stack HARD fleet-wide. New Stop floor per-turn-hard-gate.sh floors Input Routing + Depth on no-tool turns; codex-consult-gate.sh at Depth>=3 degrades to pass without the codex binary; /core:start contract expanded 4->9 blocks, gated behind onboarding so enforcement never precedes the contract. + v2.39.20 (2026-07-08) - Testlify field-incident fix: blueprint-check.sh HARD-blocked Write even after a correct prose BLUEPRINT, because the hook reads ONLY the .claude/blueprint-registered marker and no fleet-visible surface said to write it — the model's only advertised exit (BLUEPRINT_ACK=1, unusable on Write calls) taught a Bash bypass of the gate. per-turn-discipline-prompt.sh now states the marker contract (write the marker via the Write tool with HAS_OUTPUT/HAS_VERIFY/HAS_PER_STEP_VERIFY) before the first Edit/Write of each turn, and blueprint-check.sh gains an out-of-repo guard: absolute paths outside $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (e.g. ~/.claude/** memory files, sibling repos) are out of scope — they could never match any whitelist and were blocked by accident. Inside-repo enforcement unchanged; tests 6/6. (#78 depth-gate + error-text split ships separately; A4 text-validation via #73.) + v2.39.19 (2026-07-06) - #63 fix: /core:start now DOCUMENTS the H-Sutra header contract it enforces — the header format (DIRECTION/VERB/TIMING/CHANNEL/REV/RISK) is written into CLAUDE.md as its own section, closing the invisible-rule gap that caused repeated 'redo with the header' blocks. After update, re-run /core:start to regenerate the block. (A4 block-text validation ships separately via #73.) + v2.39.18 (2026-06-30) - loop-budget-guard per-turn reset + agent-orchestration exemption: fixes the session-wide 'tool-budget guard hard-stopped further file reads' deadlock. The guard's call counter was cumulative-per-session and never reset, so a long working session crossed the 250 ceiling on ordinary Bash/Read/Write calls and hard-stopped itself. New loopguard-turn-reset.sh (UserPromptSubmit) truncates the counter at the start of each real user turn (budget is now per-turn; a 250-call runaway in one turn still blocks; synthetic turns skipped). Agent/Task/Workflow dispatches are exempt (a fan-out is not a loop). (A4 block-text validation lands separately via PR #73.) Operating system for building with AI. See CHANGELOG.md.
